title: Read the Snippet
blurb: What does this line do, and which identifier does it — with the close-name impostor sitting right next to it?
traps: SpeechConfig holds credentials and voice settings; AudioConfig picks the input/output device; neither one recognizes or synthesizes on its own.
AIProjectClient.get_openai_client() is a method call on an instance, not a class-level call — the exam's documented trap.
input_audio is a message content part for spoken INPUT; modalities+audio is a request-level setting for spoken OUTPUT — they are opposite directions on the same call.
A multimodal chat deployment reads image content parts as input; ImageAnalysisClient is a separate Vision SDK with its own endpoint and fixed feature set — different services entirely.

items.label: Connects your code to a Foundry project using an endpoint and credential (package azure-ai-projects)
items.why: AIProjectClient(endpoint, credential) is the project entry point; get_openai_client() hangs off it — remove auth and this is the line that breaks.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Foundry SDK quickstart (azure-ai-projects)

items.label: Given the deployment name and a system-plus-user message array, returns the reply you then read out of choices[0].message.content
items.why: chat.completions.create(model=DEPLOYMENT_NAME, messages=[…]) is the chat call — and model= takes the deployment name, not the base model name (histack trap #5).
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure OpenAI chat completions quickstart

items.label: Holds your Speech resource key and region, and the synthesis voice name
items.why: SpeechConfig(key, region) is configured first (e.g. speech_synthesis_voice_name='en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural'); AudioConfig handles devices, not credentials.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Speech SDK documentation

items.label: Send the user's spoken question as inline audio data inside the message content
items.why: Spoken INPUT goes in message content parts as input_audio; the response-settings twin is the documented trap.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure OpenAI audio-enabled chat completions documentation

items.label: Ask the model to answer with spoken audio: voice "alloy", format "wav"
items.why: Spoken OUTPUT is requested via modalities=["text","audio"] plus audio={"voice":"alloy","format":"wav"} on the multimodal call — the exam's exact payload.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure OpenAI audio-enabled chat completions documentation

items.label: Include a photo (URL or base64) in a chat message so the deployed gpt-4o can describe it
items.why: Visual input travels as image_url / base64 content parts to a multimodal deployment — not through the Vision SDK, which is a different service and endpoint (pair #23).
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure OpenAI vision-enabled chat documentation (image input)

items.label: Bridges an existing project client to the OpenAI-compatible client used for Responses and Conversations calls
items.why: project.get_openai_client() is an instance method called on the project object; the exam's trap is calling it on the class itself instead.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Foundry SDK quickstart (azure-ai-projects)

items.label: Called once, right after the project client is built, before the first Responses or Conversations request goes out
items.why: It is the runtime bridge that hands back the OpenAI-shaped client; the credential object only authenticates the project client, it never returns a chat client.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Foundry SDK quickstart (azure-ai-projects)

items.label: Passed with zero arguments as the credential= value so the app authenticates via signed-in Azure identity, no key typed anywhere
items.why: DefaultAzureCredential() is the keyless Entra ID credential object; AIProjectClient is what consumes it, and azure-ai-projects is only the package name, not a runtime object.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure Identity library (DefaultAzureCredential) documentation

items.label: The object az login sets up for: the client resolves your signed-in identity from it automatically at call time, no environment API key needed
items.why: The quickstart pairs az login with this credential object; get_openai_client only returns a chat client and has nothing to do with authentication.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure Identity library (DefaultAzureCredential) documentation

items.label: First command in a fresh virtual environment, before any code can open a connection to a Foundry project
items.why: The Foundry project client lives in azure-ai-projects — a frequently tested package name; the search and language SDKs are the usual distractors.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Foundry SDK quickstart (azure-ai-projects)

items.label: Listed alongside az login in the quickstart setup steps, pinned to a minimum version (>=2.0.0) before any client code runs
items.why: The documented quickstart guidance installs azure-ai-projects>=2.0.0 and runs az login — the Vision and Search packages are unrelated to the project client.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Foundry SDK quickstart (azure-ai-projects)

items.label: Constructed with an endpoint and an AzureKeyCredential before any key-phrase or sentiment call can run against plain text
items.why: TextAnalyticsClient(endpoint, credential) exposes.extract_key_phrases()/.analyze_sentiment() on raw text; the other two clients target multimodal documents and images at different endpoints entirely.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Language SDK documentation (TextAnalyticsClient)

items.label: Whichever client type exposes analyze_sentiment(documents) so each document's overall sentiment gets printed back
items.why: Sentiment and key-phrase extraction are AI Language text-analytics methods on this client; the other two operate on multimodal documents or live audio, not plain text.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Language SDK documentation (TextAnalyticsClient)

items.label: Constructed with use_default_microphone=True so a kiosk captures live voice, then passed into the recognizer's constructor as its input
items.why: AudioConfig(use_default_microphone=True) picks the input device; SpeechConfig instead holds the subscription key/region, and SpeechRecognizer is the class this object gets passed into, not the device selector itself.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Speech SDK documentation

items.label: Built from a saved filename so a recognizer reads speech from a test WAV file instead of a live microphone
items.why: AudioConfig(filename=…) is the file-backed device source; SpeechConfig carries credentials and voice name, and SpeechSynthesizer plays audio out rather than reading it in.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Speech SDK documentation

items.label: Given both a speech config and an audio config, then called to capture exactly one short spoken utterance and stop
items.why: This is the class whose recognize_once_async() captures a single utterance; SpeechSynthesizer instead speaks text out, and AudioConfig only wires up the input device.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Speech SDK documentation

items.label: Its single-utterance async call returns a result object whose.text holds the transcript of what the microphone just heard
items.why: The speech-to-text class returns result.text from recognizing live audio; the synthesizer speaks instead of listens, and the Language client only ever works on text that's already been transcribed.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Speech SDK documentation

items.label: Takes a speech config with the voice name already set, then turns a text string into spoken output through the speaker
items.why: This class's speak_text_async() plays a string aloud using the configured voice; the recognizer instead converts speech to text, and AudioConfig only selects a device.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Speech SDK documentation

items.label: After a recognizer produces a text transcript, this second object reads that same string back out loud with its own async speak call
items.why: Text-to-speech playback of the recognized reply is this class's job; the recognizer already produced the text, and SpeechConfig only stores credentials and the voice name it uses.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Speech SDK documentation

items.label: Constructed with an endpoint and key, then its single call analyzes an image URL for the READ visual feature to pull text off a photo
items.why: This Vision client's.analyze(image_url=…, visual_features=[…]) call runs OCR on general images; ContentUnderstandingClient instead returns a poller from a very different, asynchronous call shape.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Vision Image Analysis SDK quickstart

items.label: Its captioning-plus-OCR call takes the image by URL rather than raw bytes, requesting both CAPTION and READ features in one pass
items.why: This Vision client's by-URL analysis method returns fixed prebuilt features like caption and read; it has no polling step and no relation to speech capture at all.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Vision Image Analysis SDK quickstart

items.label: A claims app will hand scanned policy PDFs to a custom analyzer and read field values back — the object it constructs before anything else
items.why: Content Understanding work starts from this class — the other two are separate services with separate endpoints for plain text and general images respectively.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Content Understanding SDK quickstart

items.label: Its long-running analyze call returns a poller; calling.result() on that poller is how the app waits for the final extracted output
items.why: begin_analyze() plus poller.result() is this client's asynchronous polling pattern; the Vision client's analyze() is synchronous, and the Language client's methods take documents directly with no polling.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure AI Content Understanding SDK quickstart

items.label: The image-generation request whose response field b64_json holds the actual pixel data you decode, not a url field
items.why: A GPT-image-1 deployment returns generated image bytes in response.data[0].b64_json; a completions call returns text choices, and the Vision client only analyzes an image that already exists.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure OpenAI image generation API (gpt-image-1)

items.label: A sticker-shop generator needs cut-out art with nothing behind it, so this call passes background=transparent with output_format=png
items.why: Transparent background plus PNG output are GPT-image-1-series generation parameters; nothing in the Vision analysis or chat-completion calls accepts them.
items.citation: Microsoft Learn · Azure OpenAI image generation API (gpt-image-1)
